BiblicalUsage: A serok is a thong, a shoelatchet, and Abram swore by it: I will not take from a thread even to a shoelatchet, lest thou shouldest say, I have made Abram rich. And Isaiah promises the coming army whose latchet of their shoes shall not be broken — none weary, none stumbling, none slumbering.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the shoelatchet is the smallest thing a man can take, and Abram would not take even that from the king of Sodom — his wealth would come from God alone.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
